verses.text: Woe to the city soaked in blood! It is packed with lies and plunder; its victims never stop.
Listen—the whip cracks, wheels rattle, horses charge, and chariots bounce along.
Horsemen rush forward; swords flash and spears gleam. The slain are countless, bodies pile up, and there is no end to the corpses. People stumble over the dead.
This happens because of the endless prostitution of the seductive mistress of sorcery, who sold nations through her prostitution and families through her witchcraft.
“Look, I am against you,” says the LORD of Armies. “I will pull your skirts over your face and show the nations your nakedness, the kingdoms your shame.
“I will cover you with filth, treat you with contempt, and make you a public spectacle.
“Everyone who sees you will run away and say, ‘Nineveh is ruined! Who will mourn for her?’ Where could I find anyone to comfort you?”
Are you better than Thebes, city of Amon, surrounded by rivers and protected by water, with the sea as its rampart and the sea as its wall?
Cush and Egypt gave it strength without limit; Put and Libya were its allies.
Even so, it was taken away and sent into exile. Its little children were smashed at every street corner. Its honored people were chosen by lot, and all its important men were put in chains.
You too will become drunk and hide. You will search for a refuge from the enemy.
All your fortresses are like fig trees with ripe first fruit: shake the branches, and the figs fall straight into the eater’s mouth.
Look at your troops: they have become like women. The gates of your land stand wide open to your enemies, and fire has consumed their bars.
Draw water for the siege and strengthen your defenses. Work the clay, tread the mortar, and repair the brick kiln.
But fire will consume you there, and the sword will cut you down. It will devour you like locusts. Multiply like grasshoppers; multiply like locusts!
You have more merchants than stars in the sky, but they strip the land and fly away like locusts.

Your officials are like swarms of locusts, and your administrators like clouds of grasshoppers settling on walls on a cold day. When the sun comes out, they fly away, and no one knows where they went.
King of Assyria, your shepherds are asleep; your nobles lie resting. Your people are scattered across the mountains, with no one to gather them.
There is no healing your wound; the injury is fatal. Everyone who hears the news about you claps their hands, because who has escaped your endless cruelty?”
